Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 28, and I'm a guy. I came in because I've been having neck pain since a car accident a week ago. It's been pretty bad, like a seven out of ten, and it hurts when I move my head around.
Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the nature of your neck pain, including any associated symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness?
Patient: I'm 28, and I'm a guy. The pain is in the back of my neck, and it's not constant—it gets worse when I move my head. I've had some headaches early on, but nothing else like numbness or tingling.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or consultations with a specialist for your neck pain since the car accident?
Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging studies or gone to see a specialist for this yet. I tried some ibuprofen, and that helped a little, but I didn't go to the hospital because I didn't want the cost. The doctor just did an exam and ordered an MRI now.
Doctor: Have you experienced any radiation of pain to your arms, shoulders, or upper back? Have you noticed any changes in your range of motion or any difficulty with daily activities due to the neck pain?
Patient: No, the pain just stays in my neck. It's been hard to move my head around, and it hurts when I try to turn my neck from side to side or bend it back. It's been making it tough to do some things normally, but I can still manage most of my daily activities.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the MRI that was ordered by the doctor?
Patient: I haven't had the MRI yet, so I don't have the results. The doctor mentioned they wanted to make sure there wasn't anything more serious, like a concussion or nerve issues, but I'm still waiting on that.

Patient: I haven't had the MRI yet, so I don't have the results. The doctor mentioned they wanted to make sure there wasn't anything more serious, like a concussion or nerve issues, but I'm still waiting on that.
Doctor: Could you please provide the MRI results of the cervical spine once they are available? This will help us better understand the cause of your neck pain and determine the most appropriate next steps for your care.
Patient: I haven't had the MRI yet, so I don't have the results. The doctor mentioned they wanted to make sure there wasn't anything more serious, like a concussion or nerve issues, but I'm still waiting on that.
Doctor: Could you please provide more details about the car accident, such as whether you were wearing a seatbelt, if there was any impact to your head or neck, and if you lost consciousness at the time?
Patient: I was wearing a seatbelt, and my head and neck were jerked forward really quickly when the car hit me from behind. I didn’t lose consciousness, but I did feel a lot of sudden pain right after it happened.
